first.text: You're awake! I thought you were Hushed. Or dead. Hushed is worse — dead people don't hum.
…Is that an ember? In your HAND? Does it hurt? Can I— no. Don't let me touch it.

choice.text: You said the fog leaves things behind?
Where was that humming thing again?
I found it. The humming pebble.
The beacon needs a Remnant. Could it be the pebble?
Here. Your pebble back. The beacon didn't need it.

where.text: Shingle Point. Saltmarrow's up the boardwalk. Well — most of it. The north end's gone grey.
Don't go in the grey. You forget stuff. First little stuff, then you forget to come back.

who.text: Pell. I mend nets for Mara — she's the harbormaster. And I find things.
The fog spits stuff out on the tide. Buttons. A doll's arm. Once, a whole door. Nobody remembered whose.

offer.text: Lately it spits out things that are… warm. There's one by the big rocks, north-west. It hums.
I tried to grab it but my head went soft, like when you forget a word you just had.
You've got an ember, though. Maybe the fog can't get in your head. Will you fetch it?

accepted.text: North-west, by the big rocks. Don't stand in the grey too long, even with that thing.

still_looking.text: North-west rocks. Follow the humming. You'll know it when your teeth start to itch.

pebble_return.text: You got it! And you still know your name? …You do know your name, right?
The pebble hums against your palm. For a moment you almost know the tune: a woman's voice, a cradle rocking in a boat.
That song… Mara used to hum it. Before. She can't remember the end anymore. Nobody can.
Can I keep it? I'll put it with my lost things. It'll be safe there.

choice.text: I should hold on to it. It might matter.

gave.text: Really? …Thanks. I'll keep it somewhere dry. I'll keep it forever.

kept.text: Oh. Yeah. Okay. It's probably important. Wakebearer stuff.
Just — don't lose it, all right? Somebody should remember that song.

collection.text: The pebble hums at night. I sleep better. Don't tell Mara, she'll say I've gone soft.

ask_pebble.text: Pell's hand goes to their pocket and stays there.
If it burns, nobody gets the song. Not even the wrong way I hum it. That's what the Keeper said, right? Gone gone.

choice.text: Yes. Gone for good. I'm sorry.
Keep it, Pell. I'll find another way.

ask_pebble_truth.text: …Mara can't finish it anyway. Nobody can. Maybe a song nobody can finish is the right thing to burn.
They put the pebble in your hand and close your fingers over it, hard, like it might try to get back out.
Don't tell me when you do it. I don't want to feel it go.

pebble_back.text: You didn't— it's still humming. It's still HUMMING.
I'm not crying. It's the smoke. From the beacon. Which is really far away.

lit.text: I saw it from the harbor! Gold! The fog's gone all the way back past the wall — I can see the lofts again!
Mara's got everyone mending. Funny — nobody can say what the first knot was. Like it's on the tip of your tongue, forever.
Mara's been setting out two cups at supper. Then she stares at the second one. Is that a grown-up thing?

lit_pebble.text: The fog's gone back past the harbor wall! You did it!
I had a pebble. I know I had one. I keep reaching in my pocket and there's just… pocket.
Mara was humming at the nets this morning. Then she stopped halfway and couldn't think what she'd been humming.
Weird. Everything's so quiet at night now.
